clue.text: Fibrous material in rope across width in rolled-over timber

indicators.note: the rope-and-width piece sits in the middle of the timber word
something rolled over is turned end to end, so the timber word runs backwards

parts.note: a log is a piece of timber

indicators.note: the rope is stretched across the width, so its letters lie on both sides of it

parts.note: a lasso is a rope with a running noose

explanation.surface: Describes some fibrous stuff tangled in a rope draped over a felled tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across' is a container signal here: the rope lies across the width, wrapping it, before the whole lot sits inside the backwards timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass wool is spun glass fibre used as insulation, so it is a fibrous material.

clue.text: Fertiliser everyone can see fed to flipping old badger

indicators.note: one piece is fed into the other, so it ends up inside it
flipping turns the old-badger pair over, reading backwards

parts.note: to badger is to nag
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: Pictures some fertiliser being fed to a cantankerous old badger.
explanation.walkthrough: O + NAG 'flipping' gives GANO, and U, the film certificate meaning anyone may watch, is 'fed to' it after the G. 'Flipping' looks like a mild swear word describing the badger.
explanation.definitionFit: Guano is seabird or bat droppings, prized as a natural manure for crops.

clue.text: Isn't grass cut for 6 10?

definitions.note: the definition points to the answer to 6 and 10, a racecourse

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

indicators.note: cut means the grass word loses its final letter

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: Asks whether a mown lawn might do for a racing venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: 6 and 10 together give RACECOURSE. Aintree, near Liverpool, is the racecourse that hosts the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous English horse-racing venue, home of the Grand National.

clue.text: 6 10 abroad, tourist destination not far from 5

indicators.note: abroad here means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 6, first half of a horse-racing venue
the answer to 10, second half of a horse-racing venue

explanation.surface: Suggests a racing venue overseas, near another one, that tourists flock to.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of RACECOURSE, the answer to 6 and 10, are rearranged. Sacré-Cœur is the basilica on Montmartre in Paris; 5 is Longchamp, a Paris racecourse, so 'abroad' also fits the French surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sacré-Cœur basilica is one of Paris's major sights, in the same city as Longchamp racecourse.

clue.text: Nice skin of orca shimmering on sea, say, in deep water?

indicators.note: shimmering suggests wavering, unsettled movement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the skin of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: its outer letters are used

parts.note: spoken, sea is the same as the letter C

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the French resort; it is plain anagram fodder. 'Sea, say' is the letter C by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanic means of or belonging to the ocean, so something oceanic is found out in deep water.

clue.text: 6 10 marathon winner

definitions.note: the definition points to the answer to 6 and 10, a racecourse

parts.note: a marathon task is a long one
a champ (champion) is a winner

explanation.surface: Reads as naming the winner of a marathon, as if a runner were a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 and 10 together give RACECOURSE. Longchamp is the Paris racecourse that hosts the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe.
explanation.definitionFit: Longchamp is a celebrated horse-racing venue in the Bois de Boulogne, Paris.

clue.text: Bath, perhaps, where vulgar sounds detected behind people

indicators.note: behind places the heard word after the people word

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

indicators.note: sounds detected means what is heard, not what is written

parts.note: coarse means vulgar

explanation.surface: Suggests a bath where crude noises are noticed coming from someone's rear.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath, the Somerset city, has a racecourse. 'Bath' wants to be a tub, which fits the toilet-humour surface; the capital B is the giveaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath Racecourse, on Lansdown Hill above the city, is one example of a horse-racing track.

clue.text: Proper screens an element of bronzing — catching rays?

indicators.note: to screen is to shield or hide, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: real means proper, genuine
tin is a chemical element and a component of bronze

explanation.surface: Suggests sunbathing: a proper sun cream shields part of your bronzing while you soak up the rays.
explanation.walkthrough: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin, so tin is literally an element in it, not just a part of a suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer of the eye, so anything retinal is involved in receiving light.

clue.text: 6 10 with the cloth on rough floors

definitions.note: the definition points to the answer to 6 and 10, a racecourse

indicators.note: on joins the clergy word to the rest, which follows it

parts.note: the cloth means the clergy, so the church
feeling rough is feeling ill
to floor someone is to knock them down, so downs

explanation.surface: Reads like a priest in his vestments sprawling on rough ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Churchill Downs, in Louisville, Kentucky, is the racecourse that stages the Kentucky Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill Downs is a famous American horse-racing venue, home of the Kentucky Derby.

clue.text: Sticker on vessel has cow's head, around which written Farmer's Brew?

indicators.note: the brew is written round the head letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a whimsical name for a farmer's beer: barn ale

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags BARN ALE as an invented phrase, beer as a farmer might brew it. C, from the head of 'cow's', goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnacles are crustaceans that cement themselves to ship hulls, clinging like stickers.

clue.text: Test judgement, having turned on solicitor?

indicators.note: turned means the little word is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
a tout solicits custom, so he is a solicitor in the literal sense

explanation.surface: Sounds like a verdict going against a lawyer in some trial.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match. 'Solicitor' wants to be a lawyer; here it is anyone who solicits, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the umpire's not out decision rejects an appeal that the batsman should be dismissed.

clue.text: See 6
Endlessly fine talent, novelty

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: nice can mean fine, pleasant
a knack is a talent

explanation.surface: Reads as praising a novelty that shows endless fine talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicknack is a small ornament or trinket, the sort of trivial novelty item sold as a souvenir.

clue.text: For each person, a filled dish came unfilled

parts.note: a pie is a dish with a filling

indicators.note: unfilled means the inside letters are emptied out, leaving the outer pair

parts.note: its first and last letters are kept

explanation.surface: Pictures a meal where each diner's pie arrived without any filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece is an adverb meaning to or for each one, as in 'they paid ten pounds apiece'.

clue.text: Father supporting container filled with last of wine

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: the container holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a crate is a container

indicators.note: the last letter of the word

parts.note: its final letter is used

explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' is a verb here: to father children.
explanation.definitionFit: To procreate is to beget offspring, so to sire them.

clue.text: When massaged, a toned leg stretched

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A massage leaves a toned leg nicely stretched out.
explanation.definitionFit: Elongated means lengthened, drawn out further than usual.

clue.text: Old star with cane enslaves a minister

indicators.note: to enslave is to hold captive, so the star holds the letter inside him

parts.note: Charlie Chaplin, the silent-film star famous for his cane

explanation.surface: Pictures a cane-wielding old celebrity tyrannising a government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' wants to be a politician; here it is a church minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution such as a hospital or regiment, so a minister of religion.

clue.text: Thoroughbred bay, say, for 6 10

definitions.note: the definition points to the answer to 6 and 10, a racecourse

parts.note: thoroughbred means well-bred, of good stock
the bay is a laurel tree, and trees give wood

explanation.surface: Sounds like a bay racehorse being entered for a race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' wants to be a horse's colour; here it is the bay tree. Goodwood is a Sussex racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodwood is an English horse-racing venue in West Sussex, known for Glorious Goodwood.

clue.text: Homework covering principal rule of two

indicators.note: covering means the outer word wraps round the inner one

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work done on one's own home
arch as an adjective means chief, principal

explanation.surface: Sounds like a school homework assignment on a key rule involving two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homework' wants to be schoolwork; here it is home improvement, DIY.
explanation.definitionFit: A diarchy is government by two joint rulers, so a system of dual rule.

clue.text: Something in the fryer, I appreciate that meal served up into which last of ketchup goes

indicators.note: into which, with goes, puts the letter inside the reversed piece
goes completes the instruction that the letter is placed inside
in a down answer, served up means read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: ta is an informal British thank-you
a feed is a meal

indicators.note: the last letter of the word

parts.note: its final letter is used

explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'served up' means written upwards. Ta is an informal British thank-you, matching 'I appreciate that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep fat is the hot oil a deep fryer is filled with for frying chips and the like.

clue.text: Piano rock repulsed pretty delicate little things

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the rock word runs backwards

parts.note: slate is a kind of rock

explanation.surface: Pictures delicate trinkets recoiling from a piano and some rock music.
explanation.definitionFit: Petals are the small, fragile, often colourful parts of a flower.

clue.text: Don't stop making fun of 6 10

definitions.note: the definition points to the answer to 6 and 10, a racecourse

parts.note: to taunt someone is to make fun of them
on as in carry on: keep going, don't stop

explanation.walkthrough: This is TAUNT + ON read as one instruction to keep jeering. Taunton is the county town of Somerset, with a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Taunton has a National Hunt horse-racing venue in Somerset, England.

clue.text: A musical affair?

parts.note: an orchestral percussion instrument, and a love affair involving three people

explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a percussion instrument, and a love triangle is a romantic entanglement of three.

clue.text: Dirty coat's first darned

parts.note: its first letter is used
ruddy is a mild British expletive, like darned

explanation.walkthrough: 'Darned' looks like mended with a needle; here it is the mild oath, matching ruddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruddy is slang for filthy or grimy, covered in crud.

See 7

clue.text: Capital letter reversed lower cases?

indicators.note: trapped means the letters are held inside the longer word

clue.text: Circled by bees, the drunk kicks out
